evals.prompt: Create a standalone looping SVG that explains a router distributing three incoming requests to three workers. Use a restrained editorial style, 750×720 viewBox, a 6-second synchronized timeline, and no JavaScript. Save the SVG, a browser preview, and a validation report.
evals.expected_output: A portable SMIL SVG and preview that clearly sequence request arrival, routing, and worker activity.
expectations: The output includes a standalone SVG with a 750 by 720 viewBox, title, and description.
The SVG uses declarative SMIL animation and contains no script or inline event handlers.
Related animations use a synchronized 6-second timeline.
A self-contained HTML preview is generated.
The pure-svg validation report contains zero errors.

evals.prompt: Build a reusable React TypeScript component for an animated four-step onboarding flow. It may render more than once on a page, needs play/pause/replay controls, honors reduced motion, and accepts labels as props. Include a simple usage example and validate any extracted SVG reference file.
evals.expected_output: A reusable TSX component with collision-safe SVG IDs, accessible controls, reduced-motion behavior, and example usage.
expectations: The React component uses TypeScript props for labels and playback configuration.
Any SVG definition IDs are unique per component instance.
Play, pause, and replay controls are keyboard-accessible.
The component honors prefers-reduced-motion or an equivalent explicit setting.
The output includes a usage example and no unnecessary animation dependency.

evals.prompt: Make a WeChat-compatible animated SVG explainer showing a document moving through review, revision, and approval. It should loop passively, use a static raster background URL supplied as https://example.com/background.jpg, and remain understandable if animation freezes. Produce source, preview, and a WeChat-profile compatibility report.
evals.expected_output: A conservative inline SMIL SVG that uses the supplied image URL, avoids unsupported web features, and has a useful first frame.
expectations: The SVG contains no JavaScript, foreignObject, CSS keyframes, transitions, or inline event handlers.
The passive loop uses animate or animateTransform with an intentional synchronized duration.
The supplied raster URL is used and the external-resource caveat is reported.
The first frame communicates the workflow even if animation does not play.
The WeChat validation report contains zero errors.

evals.prompt: Inspect and repair the supplied broken.svg for use as a standalone animated SVG. Preserve its visual intent, fix duplicate IDs and broken references, add accessibility metadata and reduced-motion consideration, then provide before/after validation reports and a preview.
evals.expected_output: A minimally changed repaired SVG with documented fixes, clean validation, and a preview.
expectations: The original input file is preserved and a repaired copy is created.
Duplicate IDs and unresolved references are fixed.
The repaired SVG includes a viewBox, title, and description.
Before and after validation reports demonstrate the improvement.
The repaired pure-svg validation report contains zero errors.
